clue.text: Convolvulus is a nuisance, you and I would say

parts.note: a bind is an informal word for an irksome chore or nuisance

indicators.note: say signals that the contraction is to be heard, not spelt, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: contracted, 'you and I would' is we'd

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that convolvulus is a pest, as any gardener would agree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you the contraction WE'D is only heard: its sound gives the second half of the plant's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Convolvulus is the botanical name for the climbing, twining weed of gardens.

clue.text: Old language harsh to your Scotsman

parts.note: ill can mean unkind or harsh, as in ill treatment
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: An ancient tongue sounds rough to a Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian is the Scottish form of John, so it stands for a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Illyria was an ancient Balkan region whose people spoke an extinct tongue.

clue.text: A backer of plans proving attractive to the committee?

parts.note: drawing in the sense of pulling in, as a crowd-drawing event is attractive
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A supporter of schemes wins over the committee.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is literal: an architect's plans rest on this, so it backs them.
explanation.definitionFit: A draughtsman pins plans onto a large flat surface, which supports them from behind.

clue.text: Staff member's gambit, dividing half of them with ease, say

definitions.note: the 's is short for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: dividing means splitting another piece by going into its middle
half of means the second two letters of the four in them
say signals a pair of letters heard as the word ease

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EE
a gambit is a tactical move or ploy

explanation.surface: A worker's ploy splits the group while seeming easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff member's' reads as a possessive with 'gambit', but the 's is just 'is'. 'say' and 'dividing' are the indicators: the gambit splits the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A person on a company's payroll belongs to its staff.

clue.text: Notes on one of 22 give great pleasure

parts.note: D and E are musical notes
22 across is the plural of the word for a grid entry, so one of them is the singular

explanation.surface: Musical notes on one of the lamps give joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 across answers 'lights'; one of them is a light.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrill or charm someone is to please them greatly.

clue.text: Literary person's observance in an old area of Yorkshire

definitions.note: the 's is short for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: in places the ceremony inside the abbreviation for the old district

parts.note: WR stands for the West Riding, a former division of Yorkshire
a rite is a ceremonial observance

explanation.surface: An author's ritual is held in a historic part of Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire, a large English county, was once split into three Ridings; the old abbreviation for the West Riding is the outer piece here.
explanation.definitionFit: An author is a literary person who produces books.

clue.text: Part of the ship where Jacks are found

explanation.surface: Sailors, called Jack tars, are found on board.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's floor level is one; a pack of cards, which includes jacks, is another.

clue.text: Involve popular king in international match

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: in places the king's cipher inside the match

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket or rugby match
ER is Edwardus Rex, a royal cipher for King Edward

explanation.surface: Engaging a well-liked monarch in a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is a full international match in cricket or rugby. ER is usually the Queen, but here Edward Rex.
explanation.definitionFit: To interest someone in a scheme is to get them involved in it.

clue.text: Continental princess adopts English name

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the princess takes a letter inside her

parts.note: Europa was the Phoenician princess carried off by Zeus in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A royal from the Continent takes on an English name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopts' puts E inside EUROPA, giving EUROPEA; N follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Continental in the British sense means from mainland Europe.

clue.text: Female education administrators make this six-footer jumpy

parts.note: an LEA was a British local education authority, the council body running schools

explanation.surface: School bureaucrats are accused of making some creature nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: An LEA (local education authority) was the British council body running state schools. The definition is a jumping insect with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect has six legs and this parasite is famous for leaping, so it is a jumping six-legged creature.

clue.text: It may not be stationery, so-called, but it is used for communications

definitions.text: It may not be stationery, so-called, but it is used for communications

parts.words: It may not be stationery, so-called, but it is used for communications
parts.note: the 'so-called' nudges the reader to hear stationery as stationary: a portable radio set used on the move, not paper, though it carries messages

explanation.surface: A remark that something used to communicate is not writing paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Stationery (paper) sounds like stationary (not moving); this handheld radio is carried about while talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A handheld two-way radio lets people talk while moving, so it is mobile rather than fixed equipment.

clue.text: Student also gets a gin sling, coming ashore here

parts.note: L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates
and means also

indicators.note: to sling is to throw about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A student also orders a gin cocktail on landing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sling' looks like the gin drink, but it rearranges GETS A GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A jetty or floating platform where boats moor is where passengers step onto the shore.

clue.text: The disposition of a French marshal when a child?

parts.note: a kid is an informal word for a child
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: Asking what a famous French soldier's temperament was like in his boyhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidney in the old figurative sense means temperament or sort, as in 'a man of that stamp'.

clue.text: Hear a gun, maybe, so speak loudly

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of the phrase are one possible arrangement, to be reshuffled

explanation.surface: Hearing gunfire, one raises the voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' signals that the letters of HEAR A GUN are to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To rant at length is a ranting tirade delivered forcefully to an audience.

clue.text: Rebuffed for rejecting food and sleeping accommodation

indicators.note: rejecting means throwing back, so the word for food is read in reverse

parts.note: buns are small bread rolls or cakes, an example of food
a bed is where one sleeps

explanation.surface: Someone turned away refused both the meal and a place to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns the food word back to front, which happens to give a word for rebuff.
explanation.definitionFit: To be snubbed is to be coldly turned away or slighted, which is what being rebuffed means.

clue.text: Devious Chinese dynasty supporting southern revolutionary

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means placed below the other pieces

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary
the Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644

explanation.surface: A crafty Chinese dynasty is said to back a southern rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts MING below S + CHE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A plotting person is crafty and underhand.

clue.text: Honest music-maker

explanation.surface: Describes a principled musician.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstanding person is honest; an upright is also a piano with a vertical frame, an instrument for making music.

clue.text: College obtained about fifty, translated into many languages

parts.note: a poly was a British polytechnic college

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for obtained surrounds fifty's letter

parts.note: got means obtained
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A college gets about fifty texts translated widely.
explanation.walkthrough: A poly is a former British polytechnic. 'about' puts L inside GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A multilingual edition or person spans numerous tongues.

clue.text: Wearing stockings, you once put your bloomers here

indicators.note: wearing means being clothed in, so the old pronoun sits inside the stockings

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings
thou is the old form of you

explanation.surface: Wearing stockings, you once put your bloomers here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like underwear, but it means flowers: a glasshouse is where they grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated glasshouse is where tender flowering plants are grown.

clue.text: Spectacle makes us gasp? About time

indicators.note: about means going round, so the breathing word surrounds the period

parts.note: to pant is to gasp for breath
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A show leaves us breathless for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites reading 'gasp' as amazement at the show, but it is the breathing word that goes about the period.
explanation.definitionFit: A public parade or costumed show is a grand display.

clue.text: Steps taken by godly queen introducing an interdict

indicators.note: introducing here means taking something into the middle of the goddess's name

parts.note: Hera was queen of the gods in Greek myth
an interdict is a prohibition, a ban

explanation.surface: A pious queen takes measures by issuing a prohibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' places the prohibition inside the goddess. The definition is a Cuban dance, so 'Steps' means dance steps, not stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban dance is performed in a particular set of steps, which is what the clue means by steps.

clue.text: Become known for introduction of electrical fuse

indicators.note: introduction of means the opening letter of electrical

parts.note: to fuse is to merge

explanation.surface: Something comes to light about installing an electrical fuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fuse' looks like the electrical part, but it is the verb meaning to join.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts that come out or surface become known.

clue.text: They illuminate the answers

explanation.surface: Something that throws light on the solutions.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamps illuminate; in crossword jargon the entries written in the grid are also called lights.

clue.text: A, pugnacious type somehow wielded power without it

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the power word goes round the rearranged letters

parts.note: might means strength or power

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of wielded are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fighter is said to have used his strength in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the seven letters of wielded, and 'without it' (old sense: outside) wraps the power word round them, split after its second letter. The fighter is a boxer of a weight class.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer of the class between welter and light-heavy is a fighter, a pugnacious sort.

clue.text: Charge that may have to be paid

definitions.text: that may have to be paid

explanation.surface: A fee that one might owe.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax on imports is a charge; an obligation one owes, such as respect, is paid to someone.

clue.text: Union leader embraced by member in the plant

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside, so the union's first letter goes within the limb

parts.note: a member is a limb, such as an arm

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word Union

explanation.surface: A trade unionist's boss is hugged by a member of the branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' gives U from Union; 'embraced by' puts it inside ARM.
explanation.definitionFit: A lily-like plant such as cuckoo-pint belongs to this genus.

clue.text: No information about it reacting initially to gas

indicators.note: about means going round, so NO GEN surrounds the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of reacting

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Nobody knows how a gas reacts at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information. 'initially' takes the first letter of reacting, and 'about' wraps the no-information phrase round that and 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The element making up most of the air is a colourless, odourless gas.

clue.text: Man capturing wild animal nearly fell

indicators.note: capturing means holding, so the man's name goes round the animal

parts.note: Ted is a man's name
an otter is a wild river mammal

explanation.surface: A man trapping a beast in the wild almost took a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild animal' sounds like any beast; it is the river mammal, held inside the short man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To wobble unsteadily on one's feet is to be on the point of falling.
